The operation is very simple:

1 - The first thing you will need is a glass or a regular-sized cup, preferably a transparent one.

2 - Select what you want to measure and the shape of the container, either cylindrical or rectangular. Also remember to select the thickness of the edges and the bottom. A difference of a few millimetres will result in errors of several tens of grams.

3 - Place the phone on the container.

5 - Place the phone next to the container and use your finger to choose the level of the measurement. If your phone has a cover, remove it, otherwise SUBTRACT the thickness of the cover from the thickness of the edge.

The Recipe Costing Calculator allows you to easily and quickly cost your recipes.  You enter your ingredients, and the amount you pay for them, and then you enter your recipe and it will tell you how much it will cost to make the whole thing, and how much per portion.

You can also store the instructions on how to make a recipe, along with photos, and print them out.

The app will take tax into account, and allow the user to enter the margin that they want to make so they know how much they need to charge.

Receipts can be printed from the app for sales, as well as printing recipes themselves.

The app will take automatically convert between different units of measure so even though your recipe may be in one set of units, and you buy your ingredients in another set it will know what you are spending.

The app allows you to keep track of stock, and will enable you to create shopping lists to cook various ingredients based on what you have left in stock and what you want to cook.

BrewBear is a brewer's best friend when it comes to calculations and conversions. This nifty pocket calculator lets you perform common brewing calculations in an intuitive way. Simply slide to set your variables and immediately see the outcome.

BrewBear allows you to perform the following conversions:
• Specific gravity:  SG / Plato / Brix
• Temperature:  Celsius / Fahrenheit
• Weight:  Grams / Ounces / Pounds
• Volume:  Liters / US Gallons / Imp. Gallons
• Color:  EBC / SRM / Lovibond

and these calculations:
• Mash Volume
• Evaporation / Dilution
• Attenuation (ABV, ABW and Apparent Attenuation)
• SG Correction
• Hop Substitution

For each calculation, every part of the equation can be a variable. For instance, you can calculate the mash volume given your grist weight and liquor volume (or mash thickness), but you can also calculate your grist weight if you know your target mash volume. Likewise, if you're aiming to brew a 5% ABV beer, you can easily see what your original gravity must be for a given final gravity, or vice versa. 

All that, for less than the price of a beer!

BrewBear is developed by a passionate beer brewer and software developer form the Netherlands.
